messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Canary rollout 2026-11-17T14:21Z for service=router returned elevated 5xx rate (current 8.7%, baseline 0.6%). Deploy id: deploy-20261117-879. See: https://console.redwood.ai/observability/deploys/deploy-20261117-879 :rotating_light:
Alice R: seeing this too, paged oncall. Is this only the canary (10%) or larger rollout?
Ben S: can confirm canary only. Traffic slice=canary-us-west (10%). Error spikes coincide with recent routing change in that build.
Carlos M: logs show repeated NPE in routing table lookup, stack: router.lookup -> routeCache.get -> null pointer. Quick snippet from logs:
```
2026-11-17T14:20:45Z ERROR router: null pointer at routeCache.get(RouteId)
2026-11-17T14:20:46Z ERROR router: failed to route request 500 user_id=... ctx=canary
```
Diane L: ok, this looks like feature flag "new-routing" propagation bug. I'm going to flip the FF to off for canary.
Diane L: running toggle:
```bash
curl -X POST "https://flags.redwood.ai/api/toggles/new-routing/rollback" -H "Authorization: Bearer $FF_TOKEN" -d '{"environment":"canary-us-west","state":"off"}'
```
Diane L: toggled off for canary-us-west. Waiting 30s for config propagation.
Alice R: noted. Can someone validate traffic? Oncall, can we get a canary-level synthetic to check 200s?
Oncall SRE: running synthetic now, results inbound. Also checking metrics on KV cache and routeCache warmup.
Oncall SRE: synth => 200 after flag off. 5xx dropped from 8.7% -> 0.5% over 90s window.
Ben S: great, but I still see elevated latency on a small subset (~0.4%) due to stale routeCache entries. Proposing: either force cache flush on canary hosts or proceed rollback of the canary build. Thoughts?
Carlos M: cache flush is less risky if we can target canary hosts. Command to flush (internal):
```
ssh canary@canary-host-01 "sudo systemctl restart router && /usr/local/bin/route-cache flush"
```
Diane L: prefer rollback to be safe and get us back to green fast. I can initiate rollback if oncall agrees.
Alice R: agreed, priority is customer impact. Which customers are exposed? Ops -> any support alerts?
Oncall SRE: quick customer check: no enterprise SLAs hit. A small number of API clients in us-west had failed requests (estimated ~320 requests in last 10m). No billing impact. Flag rollback mitigated most of it; but I'll still run a full rollback to be safe.
Diane L: initiating rollback to previous stable deploy:
```
redwood deploy rollback --id deploy-20261117-879 --to deploy-20261110-stable --region us-west --force
```
Diane L: rollback job submitted. Jenkins job #deploy-rollback-661 started. Link: https://ci.redwood.ai/job/deploy-rollback-661
incident-bot: NOTE: rollback job started by Diane L (job: deploy-rollback-661). Estimated 3m to complete, automated smoke after completion.
Oncall SRE: rollback completed at 14:26:02Z. Smoke shows 200s stable, 5xx down to baseline. Monitoring for regressions.
Ben S: validating dashboards — error budget markers clear. No increase in other regions.
Carlos M: leaving a postmortem todo: root cause looks like FF propagation + routeCache null-handling. Need a fix to guard against nulls and to add canary rollout health checks.
Alice R: agreed. Action items: 1) Hotfix for null-check in routing (Carlos), 2) improve FF propagation verification in rollout pipeline (Ben), 3) update runbook with cache flush steps (Oncall SRE).
Diane L: handing off to next oncall (starting 14:30Z) — summary:
- Impact: small fraction of canary traffic, ~320 failed API calls, no SLAs breached.
- Mitigation: feature flag flipped off -> reduced 5xx; full rollback performed.
- Next steps: hotfix + rollout pipeline tests + runbook update.
Diane L: @Oncall SRE can you take post-rollback monitoring and customer comms if we see any ripple?
Oncall SRE: will monitor for 30m and escalate if anything else pops up. Posting incident ticket: INC-20261117-42.
Alice R: thanks team. Closing active pager. :thumbsup:
